name: Tokyo–Yokohama telegraph service
summary: A telegraph service linking Tokyo and Yokohama, which NTT dates to 1870, brought fast electric messaging to two of Japan's main cities.
description: Telegraph service linking or serving Tokyo and Yokohama in 1870.
tier_reason: A specific community-facing use or availability in electrical communication, power or computing.
why: The new Meiji government was adopting Western technology to modernise the country, and Yokohama was the main treaty port linking Japan to foreign trade.

date.basis: Evidence for this dated community entry; not necessarily the first possible use.

events.statement: NTT dates telegraph service in Tokyo and Yokohama to 1870.
events.caveats: NTT gives 1870. The National Diet Library gives 14 September 1869; a Kanagawa prefectural history instead dates construction of the Tokyo–Yokohama line to March 1870. The conflict and exact public tariff remain unresolved.

evidence.supports: NTT dates telegraph service in Tokyo and Yokohama to 1870.
The National Diet Library gives a conflicting 1869 date.
Distinguishes an 1869 local Yokohama line and a Tokyo–Yokohama line described as under construction in March 1870.

date.label: 14 September 1869 (disputed account)
date.basis: Date stated by National Diet Library; conflicts with other institutional accounts.

events.statement: The National Diet Library dates Tokyo–Yokohama telegraph operations to 14 September 1869.
events.caveats: Conflicts with NTT’s 1870 year and the prefectural history’s construction chronology; retain as an attributed claim, not a settled operating date.

evidence.supports: The library states the 14 September 1869 date.

earliest_record.rationale: Retains the NTT-dated 1870 operating anchor pending resolution of the conflicting National Diet Library 1869 account and Kanagawa construction chronology; it is not a settled first-use date.

caveats: Institutional sources disagree whether Tokyo–Yokohama service began in 1869 or 1870; see attributed events and evidence. Public tariff remains unassessed.

research.note: Conflicting institutional chronologies require historical source reconciliation; no earlier operation is asserted as settled. Independent reader checked the National Diet Library’s attributed 1869 date; the Kanagawa PDF could not be retrieved for this review, so conflicting chronologies remain unresolved.
